title: Copilot Studio: block sharing of agents that embed maker credentials
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, admin paths, sharing-limits command, default and licensing are supported. It correctly distinguishes publish-time enforcement from runtime behaviour and identifies the preview status and protection gap for already-shared agents.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; controls[0]
claims.claim: Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials is an environment-level Copilot Studio control configured in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: The **Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials** setting is an environment-level control for Microsoft Copilot Studio agents.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Copilot Studio evaluates connections and can prevent sharing or publishing when an agent violates the connection-sharing policy.
claims.quote: It lets Copilot Studio evaluate the connections used by an agent and can prevent the agent from being shared or published when a connection violates the organization's connection-sharing policy.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: An unsafe agent must use at least one connection that does not allow credential sharing.
claims.quote:
An agent is considered unsafe for sharing when both of the following conditions are true:

- The agent uses at least one connection that doesn’t allow credential sharing.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The unsafe connection must also use design-time credentials instead of asking each user to authenticate.
claims.quote: The connection uses credentials supplied at design time instead of asking each user to authenticate with their own credentials.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: As dependency-based enforcement becomes available, an unsafe called flow or agent can make its calling agent unsafe.
claims.quote: For example, an agent might call a flow or another agent that uses a nonshareable connection. As dependency-based enforcement becomes available, an unsafe dependency can cause the calling agent to be treated as unsafe for sharing.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: Connections configured to use end-user credentials are not subject to this connection-sharing restriction.
claims.quote: Connections configured to use end-user credentials aren't subject to this connection-sharing restriction because each user authenticates by using their own connection at runtime.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The configuration article documents All sharing allowed and Safe sharing enforced as the two modes.
claims.quote: The control provides two modes. Choose the mode that matches the environment's risk tolerance and rollout stage.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: All sharing allowed detects unsafe credential use and informs makers.
claims.quote: | All sharing allowed | Copilot Studio detects and informs makers about unsafe credential use, but doesn’t block sharing.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: All sharing allowed does not block sharing.
claims.quote: To provide detection and guidance without blocking, select **All sharing allowed**.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Safe sharing enforced blocks the applicable publish and share paths for unsafe agents.
claims.quote: | Safe sharing enforced | Copilot Studio blocks applicable publish or share paths when an agent is unsafe for sharing.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Makers can still edit and save unsafe agents under enforcement.
claims.quote: When **Safe sharing enforced** is selected, makers can still edit and save an unsafe agent, but they can't newly share it.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Enforcement prevents newly sharing unsafe agents.
claims.quote: When **Safe sharing enforced** is selected, makers can still edit and save an unsafe agent, but they can't newly share it.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: A violating agent cannot be shared with everyone in the organisation for end-user access.
claims.quote: Similarly, you can't share the agent with everyone in your organization for end-user access.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: For channels without a separate Share action, enforcement occurs primarily at publishing.
claims.quote: Some channels make an agent available as part of publishing and don’t provide a separate **Share** action. In these scenarios, enforcement occurs primarily when the maker publishes the agent.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: In publish-based distribution, runtime use of the maker's user credentials can disable publishing while enforcement is active.
claims.quote: If the agent uses the maker’s user credentials at runtime, Copilot Studio marks the agent as unsafe and disables publishing while enforcement is active.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: An authenticated agent that has not been shared can publish successfully.
claims.quote: For authenticated agents, an agent that you didn't share can publish successfully, while an agent you already shared with another user is blocked from publishing when enforcement applies.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: A later publish of an already-shared agent can be blocked if unsafe maker credentials remain.
claims.quote: A later publish of an already-shared agent can be blocked if the agent still contains unsafe embedded maker credentials.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Approved system identities such as service principals, API keys or managed identities permit publishing when the connection supports the scenario.
claims.quote: Agents that use an approved system identity, such as a service principal, API key, or managed identity, can be published when the associated connection supports the scenario.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Enforcement does not retroactively unshare or disable existing shared agents.
claims.quote: Enabling enforcement doesn’t retroactively unshare or disable agents that were previously shared.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Scope
claims.claim: The control governs sharing and publishing rather than blocking an agent while it runs.
claims.quote: The sharing agents with embedded maker credentials control governs sharing and publishing. It doesn’t block an agent while the agent is running.
